personality_traits: In denial about his own emotions; claims 'I don't really get emotional about things' while visibly proving the opposite
Stoic/deadpan facade - long droopy face and downturned mouth stay almost fixed throughout, even as he cracks
Secretly sentimental about football, exposed as a soft-hearted fan hiding behind a composed exterior
Passive under his wife's gentle interrogation - doesn't argue back, just absorbs the callout
emotional_range: suppressed grief breaking through as a single tear
expressions: 0:00 heavy-lidded, neutral deadpan stare while being warned not to get emotional
0:02 slight surprised eyebrow raise on 'Me?' as he deflects the accusation
0:06-0:10 eyes widen slightly and mouth drops open as his wife recounts the lost match, expression tightening into embarrassment
0:11-0:13 single blue tear rolls down his cheek while his mouth stays in the same flat frown - stoic face literally leaking emotion he denied having
gestures: Sits leaned back in his chair with arms resting loosely on the table, one hand near his coffee cup - relaxed, unbothered posture at first
Head tilts slightly toward his wife when questioned, minimal body movement overall - he never gets up or turns away

characters.interactions_notes: The husband and wife face each other across a kitchen island, both seated with coffee cups, in a static two-shot for the whole scene. He is the target of her calm, itemized 'evidence' (team followed a month, lost on penalties, sat in the dark with a cushion), and he never verbally rebuts her - the power dynamic favors her knowing, matter-of-fact delivery over his weak denial. The tear at the end is the visual punchline that undercuts his opening line, with the wife's placid coffee-sipping continuing uninterrupted as if she expected this outcome all along.

personality_traits: Dry, observant, and matter-of-fact - delivers pointed specifics ('a team you followed for one month', 'sat in the dark holding a cushion') without raising her voice
Playfully needling/teasing rather than angry - she is amused and vindicated rather than upset
Composed and unbothered, functions as the calm 'straight man' setting up her husband's emotional reveal
Keeps receipts - remembers precise, slightly absurd details of his behavior, suggesting she pays close attention to him
expressions: 0:00 mild, almost warning look while sipping coffee as she tells him not to get emotional
0:06-0:10 eyebrows lift slightly, mouth opens as she lists the specific evidence of his meltdown, tone light and knowing rather than accusatory
0:11-0:13 continues sipping her coffee calmly while he tears up, unfazed - her expression stays composed, confirming she predicted this reaction
gestures: Holds her coffee cup at chest height for most of the scene, taking small sips between lines
Sits upright with good posture, hands resting near her cup on the table - controlled, composed body language throughout
Maintains steady eye contact with her husband while speaking, no fidgeting
characters.interactions_notes: She initiates and drives the conversation, calmly listing specific proof of her husband's emotional over-investment in football while he can only offer a weak 'Me?' in response. Her continued coffee-drinking and level tone as his tear falls signal she holds the conversational upper hand and isn't surprised by the outcome - a light, teasing spousal dynamic rather than a confrontational one.
